candidate.title: Missing credentialId branch fans out over all credentials per destination, creating duplicate external calendar events
reports: packages/core/eventmanager.ts:376 — when several destinations have no credentialid, each one re-runs createevent on every organizer credential of that integration type, which creates duplicate external events and wastes api calls

packages/core/eventmanager.ts:376 — for each destination entry lacking credentialid, events are created in all organizer credentials of that integration type, so multiple such entries in the new array create duplicate events in the organizer's calendars.

packages/core/eventmanager.ts:374 — the no-credentialid else branch now runs per destination, calling createevent on every credential of that integration type for each destination, yielding n destinations x m credentials duplicate external events (p2, conf 50)

packages/core/eventmanager.ts:377 — for a secondary host's destination calendar with no credentialid, the fallback creates the event on every organizer credential of that integration type, so the organizer gets duplicate events and the secondary host gets none.

packages/core/eventmanager.ts:374-381: destinations without credentialid fan out to every credential for the integration while omitting destination.externalid, causing google events to be created on primary calendars and references to lack calendar ids for later updates or deletions.

[low/bug] packages/core/eventmanager.ts:~382 — for destinations without credentialid, events are created on all credentials of that integration type; with multiple credential-less destinations of the same type (now possible), each credential creates an event per destination → duplicate calendar events.
candidate.example: iterating multiple destination calendars with the same integration type but no credentialid can create duplicate calendar events per credential (eventmanager.ts:337-338)

fix_scope: minimal fix for the demonstrated instance only

sibling_instances.note: other instances of this class are unverified siblings; fix.patch does not address them
